chapters.summary: Paul charges Timothy to guard against false teaching, and testifies that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, offering himself as an example of one who obtained mercy.
keyPoints: Paul reminds Timothy to remain at Ephesus, charging certain people not to teach other doctrine, nor to give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which give rise to disputes.
The law was made for the lawless and disobedient, but the gospel is glorious; Paul thanks the Lord who strengthened him, for though he had once been a blasphemer and a persecutor, he obtained mercy.
Paul holds himself up as the chief of sinners who yet obtained mercy, showing that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners - a saying faithful and worthy of full acceptance.
chapters.application: Let us follow Paul's example: acknowledge that we are sinners, yet trust firmly in Christ's salvation. Hold fast to faith and a good conscience, keep away from fruitless arguments, and carry the gospel to others.

chapters.summary: Paul urges believers to pray for all people, and instructs women on their conduct within the church.
keyPoints: He urges believers to pray for kings and all who are in authority, so that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness.
He emphasizes that God desires all people to be saved, and that Jesus Christ is the one mediator between God and man.
He instructs women to be modest and self-controlled, adorning themselves with good works, and to learn quietly.
chapters.application: Let us make it a regular habit to pray for others, since God desires all people to be saved. In church and at home, let us live out a godly witness with a gentle and quiet spirit.

chapters.summary: This chapter sets out the qualifications for church leaders - bishops and deacons - emphasizing their character and management of their households, and identifies the church as the pillar and ground of the truth.
keyPoints: A bishop must be blameless, the husband of one wife, temperate, self-controlled, respectable, given to hospitality, and able to teach.
Deacons likewise must be dignified, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy for dishonest gain, holding the mystery of the faith with a pure conscience.
The church is the household of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth, and the mystery of Christ's coming in the flesh is the foundation of godliness.
chapters.application: Whether or not we hold a position of leadership, let us all pursue good character, live out our witness in our homes and in the church, and become pillars of the truth to the glory of God.

chapters.summary: Paul warns Timothy to guard against those who depart from the true faith, and teaches him how to be a good minister of Christ, training himself in godliness and holding fast to the truth.
keyPoints: The Spirit expressly says that in the latter times some will depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits and the doctrines of demons.
Training in godliness benefits both this life and the life to come; Timothy is to hold fast to eternal life and labor for the sake of the gospel.
No one should look down on Timothy for his youth; instead he must be an example to the believers in speech, conduct, love, faith, and purity.
chapters.application: In your life of faith, give attention to training yourself in godliness, equip yourself with the truth, and be a good example in word and deed - never let your youth become an excuse to neglect responsibility.

chapters.summary: Paul teaches Timothy how to shepherd believers of different ages and standing within the church, with particular emphasis on caring for widows and on the qualifications and responsibilities of church elders.
keyPoints: He urges Timothy to treat believers of every age as family, older and younger alike, with a pure heart.
He sets out in detail the conditions for the church's support of widows, and encourages younger widows to remarry.
He teaches how to honor and support elders, and how to handle accusations brought against them.
chapters.application: Let us honor one another within the church and genuinely care for those in need, especially widows and those who labor hard in preaching, living out our faith with godliness and love.

chapters.summary: Paul urges believers to honor their masters, to pursue godliness and contentment, and to keep away from disputes and the love of money, and he charges Timothy to fight the good fight for the true faith.
keyPoints: Believers should honor their masters, whether or not those masters are believers, and serve them faithfully.
Godliness with contentment is great gain, and the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil - these things are to be fled from.
Timothy is to hold fast to the true faith, charge the rich to do good, and be firmly rooted in good works.
themes: A Warning Against the Love of Money
chapters.application: Today, let us find our contentment in godliness rather than in material things, keep a thankful heart, glorify God in our work and daily life, and bear bold witness to the truth.
